newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle closes mixed, feeders lower. [CORRECTED 20:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle closes mixed, feeders lower. [CORRECTED 20:05 GMT]

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mixed with the recent strong advance temporarily stalling as the market waited to see if forecasts for higher cash prices this week will be fulfilled, traders said.
They noted aggressive late selling of the December contract by Merrill Lynch contributed to a weak finish.
Cash cattle trade was at a standstill Monday with a few bids at $62.00 per cwt, steady with sales late last week, while offers ranged from $64.00 to $65.00.
Some dealers expected trade, when it finally develops, to be in the $63.00 to $64.00 per cwt area.
"It looks like we will be higher on the cash cattle this week but we've been up (on futures) for three days and there is not much news," one dealer said.

August live cattle closed 0.325 cent a lb lower at 65.425 cents per lb. Prices rose sharply late last week after closing on Tuesday at 62.925 cents and Monday's high of 65.900 cents was the August contract's highest level in two months.

The market's strength had been partly prompted by talk that beef prices could be poised to strengthen. USDA reported, however, as of 1130 CDT Monday, that boxed beef cut-out values were $0.07 lower to $0.15 higher in thin volume.
